items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Ulysses Livington lived not far from me at 155th Street and St. Nicholas Avenue, so we became very good friends.

ctx.x: I had a very good friend who was my favourite playmate. He lived on Barr Street but spent most of his playing time on Hathaway Street. His name was Edward Partridge and we remained friends after we grew to be men. Eddie and I used to draw pictures of horses and cowboys. Our dream was to go west and get a job on some ranch. There was one thing that puzzled me about Eddie's family it seemed that every six months at least, there was a new baby born at his house. I never knew how many brothers or sisters he had.

My father and mother seperated again and my father took me and my youngest brother Ulysses to Kentucky for a while. My brother Robert died when I was 13 years old. My sister was left with my mother and my heart was broken when I had to leave Cincinnati because apart from drawing cowboy pictures with my pal, Eddie Partridge, we had started playing with electric trains. Eddie had an after-school job in a shop that sold miniature trains and now and then he would bring something to my house that we could use in the…

Aunt Amanda, her husband and her children Mattie Parks, Agnes, Frankie Belle and Thomas were caretakers on a part of the Haggins farm and I stayed with them for months. There were cows, hogs, turkeys and plenty of chickens. Aunt Amanda was saving from every angle that she could to buy her own home and if any of her children or myself wanted an egg for breakfast, we had to pay her 2 cents for it. I became a real country boy in every respect except milking
